units.en: O God, open our hearts through blessing him; ease our affairs through it; dispel our worries through it; lift our distress through it; forgive our sins through it; settle our debts through it; set right our affairs through it; bring us to our hopes through it; accept our repentance through it; wash away our misdeeds through it; strengthen our plea through it; purify our tongues through it; comfort our loneliness through it; have mercy on our estrangement through it; and make it a light before us, behind us, on our right, on our left, above us, beneath us, in our life and at our death, in our graves, at our gathering and our rising, and a shade over our heads on the Day of Resurrection. Weigh down the scales of our good deeds through it, and make its blessings continue upon us until we meet our prophet and master Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, while we are believing, reassured, joyful and glad-tidings-filled; and do not part us from him until You admit us by his entrance and shelter us in his noble neighbourhood, with those You have blessed «among the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous — and excellent are those as companions».

units.ar:
اللَّهُمَّ
إِنَّا آمَنَّا بهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَلَمْ نَرَهُ، فَمَتِّعْنَا
اللَّهُمَّ
فِي الدَّارَيْنِ بِرُؤْيَتِهِ، وَثَبِّتْ قُلُوبَنَا عَلَى مَحَبَّتِهِ، وَاسْتَعْمِلْنَا عَلَى سُنَّتِهِ، وَتَوَفَّنَا عَلَى مِلَّتِهِ وَاحْشُرْنَا فِي زُمْرَتِهِ النَّاجِيَةِ وَحِزْبِهِ المُفْلِحِينَ، وَانْفَعْنَا بِمَا انْطَوَتْ عَلَيْهِ قُلُوبُنَا مِنْ مَحَبَّتِهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَوْمَ لَا جَدَّ وَلَا مَالَ وَلَا بَنِينَ، وَأَوْرِدْنَا حَوْضَهُ الأَصْفَى، وَاسْقِنَا بِكَأْسِهِ الأَوْفَى، وَيَسِّرْ عَلَيْنَا زِيَارَةَ حَرَمِكَ وَحَرَمِهِ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تُمِيتَنَا، وَأَدِمْ عَلَيْنَا الإِقَامَةَ بِحَرَمِكَ وَحَرَمِهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إِلَى أَنْ نُتَوَفَّى.
units.en: O God, we have believed in him, may God bless him and grant him peace, without having seen him; so let us delight, O God, in both abodes in the sight of him; make our hearts firm upon loving him; employ us upon his Sunna; take our souls upon his creed; gather us in his delivered throng and his prospering party; benefit us, on the day when neither lineage nor wealth nor sons avail, by the love of him that our hearts hold within, may God bless him and grant him peace; bring us to his purest Basin; give us to drink from his most brimming cup; ease for us the visit to Your sanctuary and his sanctuary before You take our souls; and make our dwelling at Your sanctuary and his sanctuary, may God bless him and grant him peace, continue until we are taken.

units.ar:
اللَّهُمَّ
إِنَّا نَسْتَشْفِعُ بِهِ إِلَيْكَ إِذْ هُوَ أَوْجَهُ الشُّفَعَاءِ إِلَيْكَ، وَنُقْسِمُ بِهِ عَلَيْكَ إِذْ هُوَ أَعْظَمُ مَنْ أُقْسِمَ بِحَقِّهِ عَلَيْكَ، وَنَتَوَسَّلُ بِهِ إِلَيْكَ إِذْ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ الوَسَائِلِ إِلَيْكَ، نَشْكُو إِلَيْكَ يَا رَبِّ قَسْوَةَ قُلُوبِنَا، وَكَثْرَةَ ذُنُوبِنَا، وَطُولَ آمَالِنَا، وَتَكَاسُلَنَا عَنِ الطَّاعَاتِ، وَهُجُومَنَا عَلَى المُخَالَفَاتِ، فَنِعْمَ المُشْتَكَى إِلَيْهِ أَنْتَ يَا رَبِّ، بِكَ نَسْتَنْصِرُ عَلَى أَعْدَائِنَا وَأَنْفُسِنَا فَانْصُرْنَا، وَعَلَى فَضْلِكَ نَتَوَكَّلُ فِي صَلَاحِنَا، فَلَا تَكِلْنَا إِلَى غَيْرِكَ يَا رَبَّنَا، وَإِلَى جَنَابِ رَسُولِكَ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ نَنْتَسِبُ فَلَا تُبَعِّدْنَا، وَبِبَابِكَ نَقِفُ فَلَا تَطْرُدْنَا، وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْأَلُ فَلَا تُخَيِّبْنَا.
units.en: O God, we seek intercession through him with You, for he is the most esteemed of intercessors before You; we swear by him upon You, for he is the greatest one whose right is sworn by upon You; and we draw near through him to You, for he is the closest of means to You. We complain to You, my Lord, of the hardness of our hearts, the abundance of our sins, the length of our hopes, our sluggishness in obedience, and our rushing into transgressions. What an excellent One to complain to You are, my Lord! Through You we seek victory over our enemies and our own selves, so grant us victory; upon Your bounty we rely for our betterment, so do not entrust us to anyone but You, our Lord; to the presence of Your messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, we claim kinship, so do not cast us far; at Your door we stand, so do not drive us away; and You we ask, so do not disappoint us.

units.ar:
اللَّهُمَّ
ارْحَمْ تَضَرُّعَنَا، وَآمِنْ خَوْفَنَا، وَتَقَبَّلْ أَعْمَالَنَا، وَأَصْلِحْ أَحْوَالَنَا، وَاجْعَلْ بِطَاعَتِكَ اشْتِغَالَنَا، وَإِلَى الخَيْرِ مَآلَنَا، وَحَقِّقْ بِالزِّيَادَةِ آمَالَنَا، وَاخْتِمْ بِالسَّعَادَةِ آجَالَنَا. هَذَا ذُلُّنَا ظَاهِرٌ بَيْنَ يَدَيْكَ، وَحَالُنَا لَا يَخْفَى عَلَيْكَ، أَمَرْتَنَا فَتَرَكْنَا، وَنَهَيْتَنَا فَارْتَكَبْنَا، وَلَا يَسَعُنَا إِلَّا عَفْوُكَ فَاعْفُ عَنَّا يَا خَيْرَ مَأْمُولٍ، وَأَكْرَمَ مَسْئُولٍ، إِنَّكَ عَفُوٌّ غَفُورٌ رَؤُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ يَا أَرْحَمَ الرَّاحِمِينَ. وَصَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَصَحْبهِ وَسَلَّمَ تَسْلِيمًا، وَالحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ العَالَمِينَ.
units.en: O God, have mercy on our humble pleading; calm our fear; accept our deeds; set right our affairs; make our occupation obedience to You and our outcome goodness; fulfil our hopes with increase; and seal our lifespans with felicity. Here is our abasement, laid bare before You, and our state is not hidden from You. You commanded us, and we abandoned; You forbade us, and we transgressed — and nothing can encompass us but Your pardon, so pardon us, best of those in whom hope is placed, most generous of those who are asked. You are Pardoning, Forgiving, Tender, Merciful, Most Merciful of the merciful. And may God bless our master Muḥammad, and his family and his companions, and grant them abundant peace; and praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds.

works.source_en: Classical public-domain Arabic text of Imam al-Jazūlī (d. 1465), as circulated in standard editions. English: the opening devotions, intention and first part are an original translation made for this project; Hizbs 2–8 use the historical translation by Rev. John B. Pearson (Guide to Happiness, Oxford, 1907), in the public domain.

works.author: Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr
works.description_en: The celebrated ode with which Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr sought the Prophet's ﷺ forgiveness. When Kaʿb recited it before him in the mosque, the Prophet ﷺ pardoned him and cast his own mantle (burda) over his shoulders — the gift that gives this library its name. The Arabic text follows the recension transmitted in Ibn Hishām's Sīra; the English rendering is an original translation made for this project. Both are free of copyright.

sections.heading: The Qaṣīda

units.ar:
بَانَتْ سُعَادُ فَقَلْبِي الْيَوْمَ مُتَبْوِلُ
مُتَيَّمٌ إِثْرَهَا لَمْ يُفْدَ مَكْبُولُ
units.en: Suʿād has departed, and my heart today is sick with love — enthralled in her wake, a captive granted no release.

units.ar:
وَمَا سُعَادُ غَدَاةَ الْبَيْنِ إِذْ رَحَلُوا
إِلَّا أَغَنُّ غَضِيضُ الطَّرْفِ مَكْحُولُ
units.en: What was Suʿād, on the morning of parting when they marched away, but a tender young gazelle — soft-eyed, her lashes dark as if kohled.

units.ar:
هَيْفَاءُ مُقْبِلَةً عَجْزَاءُ مُدْبِرَةً
لَا يُشْتَكَى قِصَرٌ مِنْهَا وَلَا طُولُ
units.en: Slender of waist as she approaches, full-figured as she turns away — no shortness in her to complain of, and no excess of height.

units.ar:
تَجْلُو عَوَارِضَ ذِي ظَلْمٍ إِذَا ابْتَسَمَتْ
كَأَنَّهُ مُنْهَلٌ بِالرَّاحِ مَعْلُولُ
units.en: When she smiles, she bares teeth bright with gleam, like a first draught of wine tempered sweet.

units.ar:
شُجَّتْ بِذِي شَيَمٍ مِنْ مَاءِ مَحْنِيَةٍ
صَافٍ بِأَبْطَحَ أَضْحَى وَهْوَ مَشْمُولُ
units.en: Her spaced teeth are touched as though by water from a winding stream — pure, in a broad riverbed, drawn at mid-morning, cooled by the north wind.

units.ar:
تَنْفِي الرِّيَاحُ الْقَذَى عَنْهُ وَأَفْرَطَهُ
مِنْ صَوْبِ غَادِيَةٍ بَيْضُ يَعَالِيلُ
units.en: The winds sweep every mote from it, and the shower of a morning cloud has brimmed it over with white foam.

units.ar:
قِيَالُهَا خُلَّةٌ لَوْ أَنَّهَا صَدَقَتْ
بِوَعْدِهَا أَوْ لَوْ أَنَّ النَّصْحَ مَقْبُولُ
units.en: All her talk is of friendship — if only she kept her word, or if only sound counsel were ever heeded.

units.ar:
لَكِنَّهَا خُلَّةٌ قَدْ سِيطَ مِنْ دَمِهَا
فَجْعٌ وَوَلْعٌ وَإِخْلَافٌ وَتَبْدِيلُ
units.en: But hers is a friendship blended into her very blood: caprice, deceit, broken promises, and change.

units.ar:
فَمَا تَدُومُ عَلَى حَالٍ تَكُونُ بِهَا
كَمَا تَلَوَّنُ فِي أَثْوَابِهَا الْغُولُ
units.en: She never abides in any state she is in, just as the desert-ghoul keeps shifting the colours of its robes.

units.ar:
وَمَا تَمَسَّكُ بِالْعَهْدِ الَّذِي زَعَمَتْ
إِلَّا كَمَا يُمْسِكُ الْمَاءَ الْغَرَابِيلُ
units.en: She holds to the covenant she professes only as well as sieves hold water.

units.ar:
فَلَا يَغُرَّنْكَ مَا مَنَّتْ وَمَا وَعَدَتْ
إِنَّ الْأَمَانِيَّ وَالْأَحْلَامَ تَضْلِيلُ
units.en: So let not what she dangles before you and promises deceive you — wishes and dreams are sheer delusion.

units.ar:
كَانَتْ مَوَاعِيدُ عُرْقُوبٍ لَهَا مَثَلًا
وَمَا مَوَاعِيدُهَا إِلَّا الْأَبَاطِيلُ
units.en: The promises of ʿUrqūb were her pattern, and her promises are nothing but falsehoods.

units.ar:
أَرْجُو وَآمُلُ أَنْ تَدْنُو مَوَدَّتُهَا
وَمَا إِخَالُ لَدَيْنَا مِنْكِ تَنْوِيلُ
units.en: I still hope and trust that her affection will draw near — yet I doubt any grant of it will come from you.

units.ar:
أَمْسَتْ سُعَادُ بِأَرْضٍ لَا يُبَلِّغُهَا
إِلَّا الْعِتَاقُ النَّجِيبَاتُ الْمَرَاسِيلُ
units.en: Suʿād now dwells in a land that none can reach but noble, thoroughbred, fleet-running camels.

units.ar:
وَلَنْ يُبَلِّغَهَا إِلَّا عُذَافِرَةٌ
لَهَا عَلَى الْأَيْنِ إِرْقَالٌ وَتَبْغِيلُ
units.en: And only a stalwart she-camel will get there, one that keeps her stride in spite of weariness.

units.ar:
مِنْ كُلِّ نَضَّاخَةِ الذِّفْرَى إِذَا عَرِقَتْ
عُرْضَتُهَا طَامِسُ الْأَعْلَامِ مَجْهُولُ
units.en: One that sweats freely behind the ear when she strains, her drive carrying her where the trail-marks are effaced and the land unknown.

units.ar:
تَرْمِي الْغُيُوبَ بِعَيْنَيْ مُفْرِدٍ لَهِقٍ
إِذَا تَوَقَّدَتِ الْحِزَّانُ وَالْمِيلُ
units.en: She casts her gaze into the unseen with the eyes of a lone, worn camel, when the dunes and the waste shimmer with heat.

units.ar:
ضَخْمٌ مُقَلَّدُهَا فَعْمٌ مُقَيَّدُهَا
فِي خَلْقِهَا عَنْ بَنَاتِ الْفَحْلِ تَفْضِيلُ
units.en: Massive her collar-bone, powerful her forelegs — in build she outclasses the stallion's daughters.

units.ar:
غَلْبَاءُ وَجْنَاءُ عُلْكُومٌ مُذَكَّرَةٌ
فِي دَفِّهَا سَعَةٌ قُدَّامُهَا مِيلُ
units.en: Thick-necked, strong-cheeked, rugged, masculine in frame, broad in the flank, with a mile of stride ahead of her.

units.ar:
وَجِلْدُهَا مِنْ أُطُومٍ مَا يُؤَيِّسُهُ
طِلْحٌ بِضَاحِيَةِ الْمَتْنَيْنِ مَهْزُولُ
units.en: Her hide is like a sea-turtle's shell — no starved tick on her sun-bared back can subdue it.

units.ar:
حَرْفٌ أَخُوهَا أَبُوهَا مِنْ مُهَجَّنَةٍ
وَعَمُّهَا خَالُهَا قَوْدَاءُ شِمْلِيلُ
units.en: A splinter of rock: her brother is her father, of purest stock, her uncle her maternal uncle — long-backed, swift.

units.ar:
يَمْشِي الْقُرَادُ عَلَيْهَا ثُمَّ يُزْلِقُهُ
مِنْهَا لَبَانٌ وَأَقْرَابٌ زَهَالِيلُ
units.en: Ticks crawl upon her, then slip off, as if from milk or from trailing cloaks of fine weave.

units.ar:
عَيْرَانَةٌ قُذِفَتْ بِالنَّحْضِ عَنْ عُرُضٍ
مِرْفَقُهَا عَنْ بَنَاتِ الزَّوْرِ مَفْتُولُ
units.en: High-mettled, flung onward by her haunches across the open land, her elbow twisted clear of her chest-folds.

units.ar:
كَأَنَّمَا فَاتَ عَيْنَيْهَا وَمَذْبَحَهَا
مِنْ خَطْمِهَا وَمِنَ اللَّحْيَيْنِ بِرْطِيلُ
units.en: As if the stretch from her muzzle and jowls to her eyes and throat were a long palm-branch.

units.ar:
تَمُرُّ مِثْلَ عَسِيبِ النَّخْلِ ذَا خُصَلٍ
فِي غَارِزٍ لَمْ تَخَوَّنْهُ الْأَحَالِيلُ
units.en: She runs like the bare core of a palm-trunk, tufted with hair, upon an udder never drained by milking.

units.ar:
قَنْوَاءُ فِي حُرَّتَيْهَا لِلْبَصِيرِ بِهَا
عِتْقٌ مُبِينٌ وَفِي الْخَدَّيْنِ تَسْهِيلُ
units.en: High-arched of nose; in her ears, to the discerning eye, plain nobility — and softness in her cheeks.

units.ar:
تَخْدِي عَلَى يَسَرَاتٍ وَهْيَ لَاحِقَةٌ
ذَوَابِلٍ مَسُّهُنَّ الْأَرْضَ تَحْلِيلُ
units.en: She sways along on easy haunches, trailing slack folds whose touch sweeps the ground.

units.ar:
سُمْرُ الْعُجَايَاتِ يَتْرُكْنَ الْحَصَى زِيَمًا
لَمْ يَقِهِنَّ رُءُوسَ الْأُكَمِ تَنْعِيلُ
units.en: Her dark, spear-straight legs scatter the pebbles aside, with no sandals to shield them from the hilltops.

units.ar:
كَأَنَّ أَوْبَ ذِرَاعَيْهَا وَقَدْ عَرِقَتْ
وَقَدْ تَلَفَّعَ بِالْقُورِ الْعَسَاقِيلُ
units.en: As if her forelegs' return-stroke, when she sweats while the low hills are wrapped in mirage —

units.ar:
يَوْمًا يَظَلُّ بِهِ الْحِرْبَاءُ مُصْطَخِدًا
كَأَنَّ ضَاحِيَهُ بِالشَّمْسِ مَمْلُولُ
units.en: on a day when the chameleon stands roasted, its sun-bared flank as though baked in hot ashes —

units.ar:
وَقَالَ لِلْقَوْمِ حَادِيهِمْ وَقَدْ جَنَلَتْ
وُرْقُ الْجَنَادِبِ يَرْكُضْنَ الْحَصَا قِيلُوا
units.en: and the camel-driver calls to the people, while the grey locusts kick at the pebbles: 'Take your midday rest!' —

units.ar:
شَدَّ النَّهَارِ ذِرَاعَا عَيْطَلٍ نَصَفٍ
قَامَتْ فَجَاوَبَهَا نُكْدٌ مَثَاكِيلُ
units.en: were like the arms, at the height of noon, of a tall woman in her prime who rises to lament, answered by barren, oft-bereaved women —

units.ar:
نَوَّاحَةٍ رِخْوَةِ الضَّبْعَيْنِ لَيْسَ لَهَا
لَمَّا نَعَى بِكْرَهَا النَّاعُونَ مَعْقُولُ
units.en: a keener with slack upper arms who has no wits left once the wailers announce her firstborn's death,

units.ar:
تَفْرِي اللَّبَانَ بِكَفَّيْهَا وَمِدْرَعُهَا
مُشَقَّقٌ عَنْ تَرَاقِيهَا رَعَابِيلُ
units.en: slashing her breast with her palms, her gown rent to tatters from her collarbones.

units.ar:
تَسْعَى الْغُوَاةُ جَنَابَيْهَا وَقَوْلُهُمْ
إِنَّكَ يَا بْنَ أَبِي سُلْمَى لَمَقْتُولُ
units.en: The corrupters prowl about her flanks, saying: 'You, son of Abū Sulmā, are a dead man.'

units.ar:
وَقَالَ كُلُّ صَدِيقٍ كُنْتُ آمُلُهُ
لَا أُلْهِيَنَّكَ إِنِّي عَنْكَ مَشْغُولُ
units.en: And every friend I had counted on said: 'I will not keep you — I am otherwise engaged.'

units.ar:
فَقُلْتُ خَلُّوا سَبِيلِي لَا أَبَا لَكُمْ
فَكُلُّ مَا قَدَّرَ الرَّحْمَنُ مَفْعُولُ
units.en: I said: 'Clear my path — may you have no father! Whatever the Most Merciful has decreed will come to pass.'

units.ar:
كُلُّ ابْنِ أُنْثَى وَإِنْ طَالَتْ سَلَامَتُهُ
يَوْمًا عَلَى آلَةٍ حَدْبَاءَ مَحْمُولُ
units.en: Every child of woman, however long his safety lasts, is one day carried on a curving bier.

units.ar:
نُبِّئْتُ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ أَوْعَدَنِي
وَالْعَفْوُ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ مَأْمُولُ
units.en: I was told that God's Messenger had threatened me — yet pardon from God's Messenger is still hoped for.

units.ar:
مَهْلًا هَدَاكَ الَّذِي أَعْطَاكَ نَافِلَةَ
الْقُرْآنِ فِيهَا مَوَاعِظٌ وَتَفْصِيلُ
units.en: Gently — may He guide you, He who granted you the gift of the Qur'an, in which are admonitions and clear exposition.

units.ar:
لَا تَأْخُذَنِّي بِأَقْوَالِ الْوُشَاةِ وَلَمْ
أُذْنِبْ وَلَوْ كَثُرَتْ فِيَّ الْأَقَاوِيلُ
units.en: Do not seize me for the words of slanderers when I have done no wrong, though the tales about me abound.

units.ar:
لَقَدْ أَقُومُ مَقَامًا لَوْ يَقُومُ بِهِ
أَرَى وَأَسْمَعُ مَا لَوْ يَسْمَعُ الْفِيلُ
units.en: I have stood in a gathering where, had the elephant stood there — I swear I would have seen and heard it —

units.ar:
لَظَلَّ يَرْعَدُ إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ
مِنَ الرَّسُولِ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ تَنْوِيلُ
units.en: it would still be trembling, unless the Messenger, by God's leave, granted it assurance of safety.

units.ar:
حَتَّى وَضَعْتُ يَمِينِي مَا أُنَازِعُهُ
فِي كَفِّ ذِي نَقِمَاتٍ قِيلُهُ الْقِيلُ
units.en: Until I placed my right hand, not disputing with him, in the palm of the master of retributions, whose word is final.

units.ar:
فَلَهُوَ أَخْوَفُ عِنْدِي إِذْ أُكَلِّمُهُ
وَقِيلَ إِنَّكَ مَنْسُوبٌ وَمَسْئُولُ
units.en: And he is the most dreaded in my eyes when I address him — and it was said: 'You are marked and will be questioned.'

units.ar:
مِنْ ضَيْغَمٍ بِضَرَاءِ الْأَرْضِ مُخْدَرُهُ
فِي بَطْنِ عَثَّرَ غِيلٌ دُونَهُ غِيلُ
units.en: From a lion whose lair lies in the tangled growth, in the vale of ʿAththar — thicket beyond thicket —

units.ar:
يَغْدُو فَيُلْحِمُ ضِرْغَامَيْنِ عَيْشُهُمَا
لَحْمُ مِنَ النَّاسِ مَعْفُورٌ خَرَادِيلُ
units.en: who sets out at dawn to feed two lion cubs whose fare is the flesh of men, unavenged, in scattered shreds.

units.ar:
إِذَا يُسَاوِرُ قِرْنًا لَا يَحِلُّ لَهُ
أَنْ يَتْرُكَ الْقِرْنَ إِلَّا وَهُوَ مَفْلُولُ
units.en: When he assails a rival, he may not leave his foe until the foe is broken.

units.ar:
مِنْهُ تَظَلُّ سِبَاعُ الْجَوِّ نَافِرَةً
وَلَا تَمَشَّى بِوَادِيهِ الْأَرَاجِيلُ
units.en: From him the beasts of the waste keep fleeing, and no foot-travellers walk his valley.

units.ar:
وَلَا يَزَالُ بِوَادِيهِ أَخُو ثِقَةٍ
مُضَرَّجُ الْبَزِّ وَالدُّرْسَانِ مَأْكُولُ
units.en: And there lies ever in his valley a trusting soul, his garments drenched in blood, his tatters devoured.

units.ar:
إِنَّ الرَّسُولَ لَنُورٌ يُسْتَضَاءُ بِهِ
مُهَنَّدٌ مِنْ سُيُوفِ اللَّهِ مَسْلُولُ
units.en: The Messenger is a light by which one is guided — an Indian blade of God's swords, drawn.

units.ar:
فِي عُصْبَةٍ مِنْ قُرَيْشٍ قَالَ قَائِلُهُمْ
بِبَطْنِ مَكَّةَ لَمَّا أَسْلَمُوا زُولُوا
units.en: Among a band of Quraysh whose spokesman in Mecca's valley said, when they embraced Islam: 'Depart!'

units.ar:
زَالُوا فَمَا زَالَ أَنْكَاسٌ وَلَا كُشُفٌ
عِنْدَ اللِّقَاءِ وَلَا مِيلٌ مَعَازِيلُ
units.en: They departed — yet no weaklings departed among them, none shieldless at the clash, no unarmed stragglers.

units.ar:
شُمُّ الْعَرَانِينِ أَبْطَالٌ لَبُوسُهُمْ
مِنْ نَسْجِ دَاوُدَ فِي الْهَيْجَا سَرَابِيلُ
units.en: High-nosed heroes, whose armour in the fray is of David's weave — coats of mail,

units.ar:
بِيضٌ سَوَابِغُ قَدْ شُكَّتْ لَهَا حَلَقٌ
كَأَنَّهَا حَلَقُ الْقَفْعَاءِ مَجْدُولُ
units.en: white, ample, riveted with rings like the clustered rings of the thorn-tree, woven tight.

units.ar:
لَيْسُوا مَفَارِيحَ إِنْ نَالَتْ رِمَاحُهُمْ
قَوْمًا وَلَيْسُوا مَجَازِيعَ إِذَا نِيلُوا
units.en: They do not exult when their spears strike a people down, nor are they rent with grief when struck.

units.ar:
يَمْشُونَ مَشْيَ الْجِمَالِ الزُّهْرِ يَعْصِمُهُمْ
ضَرْبٌ إِذَا عَرَّدَ السُّودُ التَّنَابِيلُ
units.en: They walk with the gait of bright camels, shielded by blows when the black-livered cowards scatter.

units.ar:
لَا يَقَعُ الطَّعْنُ إِلَّا فِي نُحُورِهِمْ
وَمَا لَهُمْ عَنْ حِيَاضِ الْمَوْتِ تَهْلِيلُ
units.en: Spears find only their throats, and they never flinch from the watering-pools of death.

sections.note: Fifty-eight verses, as transmitted in Ibn Hishām's Sīra: the familiar opening to Suʿād, the camel that carried him, and the plea and praise recited before the Prophet ﷺ.

sections.heading: The Verses of the Anṣār

units.ar:
مَنْ سَرَّهُ كَرْمُ الْحَيَاةِ فَلَا يَزَلْ
فِي مِقْنَبٍ مِنْ صَالِحِي الْأَنْصَارِ
units.en: Whoever delights in a life of honour, let him stay among a squadron of the righteous Helpers,

units.ar:
وَرِثُوا الْمَكَارِمَ كَابِرًا عَنْ كَابِرٍ
إِنَّ الْخِيَارَ هُمْ بَنُو الْأَخْيَارِ
units.en: who inherited noble ways, elder from elder — the best are ever the sons of the best.

units.ar:
الْمُكْرِهِينَ السَّمْهَرِيَّ بِأَذْرُعٍ
كَسَوَالِفِ الْهِنْدِيِّ غَيْرِ قِصَارِ
units.en: Who drive home the Samharī spear with arms like the long edges of Indian blades — nothing short about them,

units.ar:
وَالنَّاظِرِينَ بِأَعْيُنٍ مُحْمَرَّةٍ
كَالْجَمْرِ غَيْرُ كَلَيْلَةِ الْأَبْصَارِ
units.en: who glare with reddened eyes like embers, their gaze never wearying,

units.ar:
وَالْبَائِعِينَ نُفُوسَهُمْ لِنَبِيِّهِمْ
لِلْمَوْتِ يَوْمَ تَعَانُقٍ وَكِرَارِ
units.en: who sell their souls to their Prophet unto death, on the day of grappling and charge,

units.ar:
وَالْقَائِدِينَ النَّاسَ عَنْ أَدْيَانِهِمْ
بِالْمَشْرَفِيِّ وَبِالْقَنَا الْخَطَّارِ
units.en: who drive men away from their false religions with the Indian sword and the quivering spear.

units.ar:
يَتَطَهَّرُونَ يَرَوْنَهُ نُسْكًا لَهُمْ
بِدِمَاءِ مَنْ عَلِقُوا مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ
units.en: They hold it an act of devotion to cleanse themselves in the blood of whichever unbelievers they catch.

units.ar:
دَرِبُوا كَمَا دَرِبَتْ بِبَطْنِ خُفَيَّةٍ
غُلْبُ الرِّقَابِ مِنَ الْأُسُودِ ضَوَارِي
units.en: They are battle-hardened as the thick-necked lions that prowl the vale of Khufayya are hardened to the hunt.

units.ar:
وَإِذَا حَلَلْتَ لِيَمْنَعُوكَ إِلَيْهِمْ
أَصْبَحْتَ عِنْدَ مَعَاقِلِ الْأَعْفَارِ
units.en: And if you camped against them, they would keep you off — you would wake amid the strongholds of ibex kids.

units.ar:
ضَرَبُوا عَلِيًّا يَوْمَ بَدْرٍ ضَرْبَةً
دَانَتْ لِوَقْعَتِهَا جَمِيعُ نِزَارِ
units.en: They struck the clan of ʿAliyy on the day of Badr a blow to which all of Nizār submitted.

units.ar:
لَوْ يَعْلَمُ الْأَقْوَامُ عِلْمِي كُلَّهُ
فِيهِمْ لَصَدَّقَنِي الَّذِينَ أُمَارِي
units.en: If the peoples knew all that I know of them, even those I dispute with would surely believe me.

units.ar:
قَوْمٌ إِذَا خَوَتِ النُّجُومُ فَإِنَّهُمْ
لِلطَّارِقِينَ النَّازِلِينَ مَقَارِي
units.en: A people who, when the stars set without bringing rain, are still a spread feast for guests who come by night,

units.ar:
فِي الْغُرِّ مِنْ غَسَّانَ مِنْ جُرْثُومَةٍ
أَعْيَتْ مَحَافِرُهَا عَلَى الْمِنْقَارِ
units.en: among the noblest of Ghassān, of a stock whose dug wells baffle the beak.

sections.note: After reciting the ode, Kaʿb was told the Prophet ﷺ wished he had praised the Anṣār too — so he added these verses in their honour.

works.source_en: Arabic text follows the recension transmitted in Ibn Hishām's Sīra. The English translation is an original rendering made for this project.

works.title_en: Ṭalaʿa al-Badru ʿAlaynā (The Full Moon Has Risen)
works.author: The people of Madinah
works.description_en: The welcome sung by the people of Madinah — tradition holds, by its young girls — as the Prophet ﷺ entered the city at the end of the Hijrah, coming over the mountain passes known as the Thaniyyāt al-Wadāʿ, the Passes of Farewell. Perhaps the oldest and most beloved devotional song in Islam.
works.source_en: Traditional text sung at the Prophet’s ﷺ arrival in Madinah, as transmitted in the sīra literature. The English rendering is original to this project.

sections.heading: The Welcome Song
sections.note: Sung at Qubā, on the outskirts of Madinah, in September 622.

units.ar: طَلَعَ الْبَدْرُ عَلَيْنَا — مِنْ ثَنِيَّاتِ الْوَدَاعِ
units.en: The full moon has risen upon us — from the Passes of Farewell;

units.ar: وَجَبَ الشُّكْرُ عَلَيْنَا — مَا دَعَا لِلَّهِ دَاعِ
units.en: and thanks is owed from us — as long as a caller calls to Allah.

units.ar: أَيُّهَا الْمَبْعُوثُ فِينَا — جِئْتَ بِالْأَمْرِ الْمُطَاعِ
units.en: O you who were sent among us — you came with a command to be obeyed;

units.ar: جِئْتَ شَرَّفْتَ الْمَدِينَةَ — مَرْحَبًا يَا خَيْرَ دَاعٍ
units.en: you came and honoured Madinah — welcome, O best of callers.

works.author: Ḥassān ibn Thābit
works.description_en: Ḥassān ibn Thābit of Madinah was the Prophet’s ﷺ own poet, given a minbar in the mosque from which to answer those who lampooned him — “Jibrīl is with you as long as you defend the Messenger of Allah.” These short pieces are among the most famous madih verses in the language.
works.source_en: Arabic texts as transmitted in Ḥassān’s dīwān and, for the minbar poem, in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim. The English renderings are original to this project.

sections.heading: The Celebrated Quatrain
sections.note: The most famous lines of prophetic praise in Arabic — Ḥassān’s eyewitness description of the Prophet ﷺ.

units.ar: وَأَحْسَنُ مِنْكَ لَمْ تَرَ قَطُّ عَيْنِي
units.en: My eye has never seen anyone more excellent than you,

units.ar: وَأَجْمَلُ مِنْكَ لَمْ تَلِدِ النِّسَاءُ
units.en: and no woman has ever borne one more beautiful than you;

units.ar: خُلِقْتَ مُبَرَّأً مِنْ كُلِّ عَيْبٍ
units.en: you were created free of every fault,

units.ar: كَأَنَّكَ قَدْ خُلِقْتَ كَمَا تَشَاءُ
units.en: as though you were created just as you wished.

sections.heading: The Defence from the Minbar
sections.note: From Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim: Ḥassān’s answer, from the minbar set up for him in the mosque, to the poets of Quraysh who lampooned the Prophet ﷺ.

units.ar: هَجَوْتَ مُحَمَّدًا فَأَجَبْتُ عَنْهُ — وَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ فِي ذَاكَ الْجَزَاءُ
units.en: You lampooned Muḥammad — and I answered for him; with Allah lies the reward for that.

units.ar: هَجَوْتَ مُحَمَّدًا بَرًّا حَنِيفًا — رَسُولَ اللَّهِ شِيمَتُهُ الْوَفَاءُ
units.en: You lampooned Muḥammad: a righteous, upright man, the Messenger of Allah, whose nature is loyalty.

units.ar: فَإِنَّ أَبِي وَوَالِدَهُ وَعِرْضِي — لِعِرْضِ مُحَمَّدٍ مِنْكُمْ وِقَاءُ
units.en: So my father, my mother, and my honour are a shield for Muḥammad’s honour against you.

units.ar: فَمَنْ يَهْجُو رَسُولَ اللَّهِ مِنْكُمْ — وَيَمْدَحُهُ وَيَنْصُرُهُ سَوَاءُ
units.en: Whoever of you lampoons the Messenger of Allah — or praises him or aids him — it is all the same:

units.ar: وَجِبْرِيلُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ فِينَا — وَرُوحُ الْقُدُسِ لَيْسَ لَهُ كِفَاءُ
units.en: Jibrīl, Allah’s messenger, is among us, and the Holy Spirit has no equal.

works.author: Various artists
works.description_en: A collection of devotional performances captured on commercial 78rpm discs in Cairo and beyond between 1905 and 1915 — tawshīḥ, qasā'id, and Quranic recitation by some of the earliest recorded voices of the Arabic gramophone era. These discs were published before 1923 and are in the public domain.

audio.title: Tawshīḥ: Fātanā shurub al-hanā
audio.label: Favorite 1-55584
audio.credit: Historic recording courtesy of the Harvard Loeb Music Library, Arabic 78 Collection.
audio.description: A tawshīḥ — a devotional poem in praise of the Prophet ﷺ sung to a measured melody — recorded in Cairo in 1905 for the Favorite label, in the very first years of commercial Arabic recording.

audio.title: Tawshīḥ: Yā ghazālān
audio.label: Favorite 1-55585
audio.credit: Historic recording courtesy of the Harvard Loeb Music Library, Arabic 78 Collection.
audio.description: A second tawshīḥ in praise of the Prophet ﷺ by Aḥmad al-Ajamī, from the same 1905 Cairo sessions for the Favorite label.

audio.title: Qasîda A-lâ fî sabîl Allâh (Pt 1)
audio.label: Favorite 2-55515
audio.credit: Historic recording courtesy of the Harvard Loeb Music Library, Arabic 78 Collection.
audio.description: The first side of a qaṣīda by the celebrated Egyptian reciter Saʿīd al-Saftī, recorded in Cairo in 1905. The poem runs across both sides of the disc — part 2 completes it.

audio.title: Qasîda A-lâ fî sabîl Allâh (Pt 2)
audio.label: Favorite 2-55519
audio.credit: Historic recording courtesy of the Harvard Loeb Music Library, Arabic 78 Collection.
audio.description: The second side of Saʿīd al-Saftī's qaṣīda — together with part 1 it makes up the complete recording, cut in Cairo in 1905.

audio.title: Qaṣīdat Allāhu akbar
audio.label: Baida 200a
audio.credit: Historic recording courtesy of the Harvard Loeb Music Library, Arabic 78 Collection.
audio.description: A qaṣīda opening with the takbīr, recorded around 1907–1911 for Baidaphon — the Beirut-based label whose discs circulated across the eastern Mediterranean.

audio.title: Hayyamatnī / Ṭayyamatnī
audio.label: Baida 245
audio.credit: Historic recording courtesy of the Harvard Loeb Music Library, Arabic 78 Collection.
audio.description: A further devotional disc by Aḥmad al-Mīr from the same Baidaphon period, around 1907–1911.

audio.title: Sūrat Yūsuf (Pt 1)
audio.label: Victor 73429-A
audio.credit: Historic recording courtesy of the Harvard Loeb Music Library, Arabic 78 Collection.
audio.description: Recitation from Sūrat Yūsuf by Wadūdah al-Minyalāwī, recorded for Victor in Cairo in 1915 — a rare surviving example of a commercially released Quranic disc by a female reciter in the 78rpm era. Part 2 carries the second side.

audio.title: Sūrat Yūsuf (Pt 2)
audio.label: Victor 73429-A
audio.credit: Historic recording courtesy of the Harvard Loeb Music Library, Arabic 78 Collection.
audio.description: The second side of Wadūdah al-Minyalāwī's 1915 Victor recording of Sūrat Yūsuf.

audio.title: Qur'an: Sūras 1, 112, 114 & 110
audio.label: Archives de la Parole (Pathé) 296
audio.credit: Historic recording courtesy of the Bibliothèque nationale de France (Gallica) — Archives de la Parole, Université de Paris. Public domain.
audio.description: Short chapters of the Qur'an recited in Paris in 1921 for the Archives de la Parole — the Sorbonne's sound archive, which documented the languages and recitation traditions of the time.

audio.title: Poem of al-Farazdaq (basīṭ metre)
audio.label: Archives de la Parole (Pathé) 297
audio.credit: Historic recording courtesy of the Bibliothèque nationale de France (Gallica) — Archives de la Parole, Université de Paris. Public domain.
audio.note: Classical Arabic poetry — content under editorial review
audio.description: A classical ode by the Umayyad-era poet al-Farazdaq, recited in the basīṭ metre and recorded in Paris in 1921 as a specimen of classical Arabic recitation for the Archives de la Parole.

audio.title: Biaini
audio.label: Archives de la Parole I.188
audio.credit: Historic recording courtesy of the Bibliothèque nationale de France (Gallica) — Archives de la Parole, Université de Paris. Public domain.
audio.description: A recording from the Archives de la Parole's North African sessions in Paris, 1914.

audio.title: Sūrat al-Fātiḥa
audio.label: Archives de la Parole I.189
audio.credit: Historic recording courtesy of the Bibliothèque nationale de France (Gallica) — Archives de la Parole, Université de Paris. Public domain.
audio.description: Sūrat al-Fātiḥa, the opening chapter of the Qur'an, recited in Paris in 1914 for the Archives de la Parole.

audio.title: Taravīḥ — Ramadan night-prayer chant
audio.label: E. Berliner's Gramophone 24023
audio.credit: Public-domain recording (1901). Transfer courtesy of Excavated Shellac (Jonathan Ward).
audio.note: Among the oldest Islamic devotional recordings known to survive — captured at Fred Gaisberg's Kazan sessions, June 1901.
audio.description: A tarawīḥ prayer chant recorded in Kazan in June 1901 during Fred Gaisberg's recording expedition for the Gramophone Company — among the oldest Islamic devotional recordings known to survive.
